title: Late Fee Rule for the Installment Payment Plans
content:
**Clause.** On the **Installment Payment Plans**, a late fee is assessed only later than the plan's grace period in calendar days after the due date of the installment, and only when that installment's minimum due is still not paid in full. Calendar days are counted from the due date as day 0; a payment posted on or before the due date plus the grace days is on time, and the fee may be assessed from the following day.

**Limit.** No more than the plan's maximum number of late fees per installment invoice (one, on every plan) is charged for one installment invoice.

**Timeliness.** Payment timeliness is judged by the posting date, except that a mailed payment whose postmark date is on or before the due date plus the grace days counts as on time.

**No late fee** is charged on the Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan, on a final bill, or on an automatic draft that cleared on its draft date.

**Evidence.** The invoice's due date and minimum due, and the payments posted against it, as the system records them; an earlier late fee linked to the same invoice bars a second one.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, grace period of 5 calendar days, due date on day 0)**

| Payment covering the minimum due | Late fee |
|---|---|
| posts on day 5 | none: on time |
| mailed, postmarked on day 5, posts on day 6 | none: the postmark counts as on time |
| none posted or postmarked by day 5, minimum due still not paid in full | may be assessed from day 6 |
| an automatic draft that cleared on its draft date | none |

A late fee already charged on the invoice means no further late fee for that invoice.
